item.title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. II. System-parameter uncertainties and overall errors
item.author: Chia-Hsien Huang, and Hsi-Sheng Goan
item.content:encoded:
In the companion paper (Part I), we developed an optimal-control framework to suppress intrinsic and decoherence-induced errors in controlled-Z (CZ) gates between directly coupled,frequency-tunable transmons. Here, we extend this framework to incorporate uncertainties in coupling strength, anharmonicities, and zero-flux qubit frequencies, enabling the design of high-fidelity gates robust against noise and parameter uncertainties. We classify these uncertainties by whether they perturb the off-diagonal coupling strengths or the diagonal detunings of the Hamiltonian, and we identify distinct suppression mechanisms for each class. Coupling errors are mitigated through dynamical decoupling induced by strong detuning modulation. For a 30-ns gate, this strategy reduces the coupling error to 6.21×10−7 and tolerates coupling-strength uncertainties up to 2π×4 MHz while keeping total gate infidelity below 10−3. Detuning errors are minimized near a symmetric-detuning operating point that balances the two dominant leakage-mediated interactions. A 24-ns gate operated near this point tolerates individual uncertainties of up to 2π×5 MHz in each relevant diagonal parameter under the same infidelity threshold. We further optimize gate performance under realistic conditions where intrinsic errors, decoherence, and parameter uncertainties coexist across six representative stages of progressively improving hardware performance. The resulting stage-specific controls achieve lower infidelity and greater robustness. Together with the companion study (Part I), this framework offers a practical approach to balance speed, fidelity, and robustness while reducing the need for exhaustive characterization and frequent recalibration in large-scale superconducting quantum processors.

Chia-Hsien Huang, and Hsi-Sheng Goan

item.title: Superconducting parametric amplifiers based on arrays of unequal Josephson junction elements
item.author: Boris Chesca, Tom Dixon, Narendra Acharya, Renuka D. Pothuraju, Jacob W. Dunstan, Connor D. Shelly, and Oscar W. Kennedy
item.content:encoded:
Impedance matching is a crucial feature of an amplifier used to increase its instantaneous bandwidth and is typically achieved using static LC resonators. Here we show an approach toimpedance matching in parametric amplifiers using arrays of unequal Josephson-junction-based elements (rf/dc SQUIDs, SNAILs, etc). The elements act either as small-footprint flux-tunable inductors forming an impedance-matching circuit, or ‚active‘ amplifier elements which result in amplifier gain. We develop an analytical theory describing these systems, predicting a quasi-non-periodic amplifier frequency and gain modulation with applied flux and the broadening of gain bandwidths. We demonstrate this in devices using arrays of flux-focused SNAILs where flux biasing varies across the array. We find instantaneous bandwidths of 200 MHz with >17 dB of gain centred at ∼5.4 GHz in a device without a static impedance matcher. This broadening of amplifier bandwidth is stable with >100 MHz bandwidth at 17 dB gain across >1.2 GHz tunable bandwidth. Our analytical model captures flux dependence and qualitatively reproduces gain-bandwidths giving confidence in our understanding of these systems and allowing operational figures of merit to be optimised in future devices.

Boris Chesca, Tom Dixon, Narendra Acharya, Renuka D. Pothuraju, Jacob W. Dunstan, Connor D. Shelly, and Oscar W. Kennedy

item.title: Meter-scale quantum interconnects between large quantum processors
item.author: Neereja M. Sundaresan, Nicholas Cotaj, Yadav Prasad Kandel, Eric Lewandowski, Christian Robert Longton, Yves Martin, Jae-woong Nah, Kathryn Pooley, Martin Sandberg, Michael Scanlon, Chi Xiong, Emanuil Sashev Yanev, David Abraham, Abhinandan Antony, Vincent Arena, Nicholas Bornman, Khanh Dang, Oliver Dial, Christopher Guarino, Gabriel Haspil, Jared Hertzberg, Kentaro Heya, Swetha Kamlapurkar, Michael Karschner, George Keefe, Eric Liniger, Laura Luo, Thomas G. McConkey, David Olson, Jason Orcutt, Dmitry Ovchinnikov, Timothy Phung, Sankeerth Rajalingam, Michael Selvanayagam, William Shanks, Dongbing Shao, Abigail Shearrow, Adam Stabile, Jiri Stehlik, Joseph Suttle, Jeng-Bang Yau, and Eric Zhang
item.content:encoded:
Modular quantum architecture requires long-distance quantum interconnects to stitch together individual processor modules. Such interconnects, long-distance couplers or L-couplers,must support coherent quantum operation over meter-scale distances and scale to multiple connections between any two modules. Here we demonstrate four L-couplers operating between two 120-qubit IBM Nighthawk R1 superconducting qubit processors. Each L-coupler joins two Nighthawk lattice qubits through two frequency-tunable L-qubits, two RF-SQUID based „i2m“ couplers, and 80 cm of superconducting aluminum coax. Each cable installs perpendicular to the processor surface, to enable denser connections, and is joined to the chip by an indium-to-indium room temperature pressure bond made after both modules were mounted. L-coupler modes near 5 GHz, with internal quality factors of 0.86 to 1.09e6, carry relay-based state transfer at a mean network benchmarking fidelity of 99.00%, with a best link of 99.29 +/- 0.07%. We then realize distant CZ gates between lattice qubits in separate modules at a mean fidelity of 94.75%, with a best link of 96.42 +/- 0.28%, and use them to generate entangled states across the two processors, including a demonstration of simultaneous Bell pair generation using two adjacent L-couplers. These four high-fidelity L-couplers establish a practical path to scalable quantum interconnects for modular quantum computing.

Neereja M. Sundaresan, Nicholas Cotaj, Yadav Prasad Kandel, Eric Lewandowski, Christian Robert Longton, Yves Martin, Jae-woong Nah, Kathryn Pooley, Martin Sandberg, Michael Scanlon, Chi Xiong, Emanuil Sashev Yanev, David Abraham, Abhinandan Antony, Vincent Arena, Nicholas Bornman, Khanh Dang, Oliver Dial, Christopher Guarino, Gabriel Haspil, Jared Hertzberg, Kentaro Heya, Swetha Kamlapurkar, Michael Karschner, George Keefe, Eric Liniger, Laura Luo, Thomas G. item.title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. I. Intrinsic errors and decoherence
item.author: Chia-Hsien Huang, and Hsi-Sheng Goan
item.content:encoded:
Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum gates that combine short duration, high fidelity, and robustness to noise. As quantum processors scale, robustness becomes increasinglyimportant because exhaustive characterization and frequent recalibration of individual gates become impractical. We present a comprehensive optimal-control framework for controlled-Z (CZ) gates between directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons that systematically accounts for intrinsic Hamiltonian errors and realistic decoherence mechanisms, including energy relaxation and dephasing. Using smooth, single-shot flux pulses, we obtain 12-ns CZ gates—close to the theoretical speed limit of 11.6 ns—with intrinsic errors suppressed to the 2×10−5 level. We construct dephasing noise models, calibrated against published experimental measurements, that capture fast dephasing from room-temperature control electronics and slow dephasing from 1/f flux noise. Using these models, we identify dephasing sweet spots that suppress sensitivity to dephasing noise. We further exploit transmon asymmetry as a design parameter to access distinct noise-resilient operating regimes. These results establish an experimentally applicable framework for balancing gate speed, fidelity, and noise robustness while reducing characterization and recalibration overhead.

Chia-Hsien Huang, and Hsi-Sheng Goan

item.title: Bias-Preserving Entanglement of Kerr-Cat Qubits with an ATS Coupler
item.author: Kerem Yurtseven, Shantanu R. Jha, Apoorva Limaye, Risav Pokhrel, and Muhammad Waqar Amin
item.content:encoded:
Kerr-cat qubits offer a hardware-efficient route to fault-tolerant quantum computing by suppressing bit-flip errors exponentially, while phase-flip errors increase only linearly withthe mean photon number. To maintain this protection, entangling operations must be bias-preserving, ensuring that phase-flip errors occurring during the gate do not propagate into bit-flip errors. In this paper, we propose an asymmetrically threaded SQUID (ATS) parametric coupler to implement high-fidelity, bias-preserving entangling gates between Kerr-cat qubits. By engineering a photon-number asymmetry between the control and target modes, we enable fast gate operations that suppress non-adiabatic leakage without complex pulse shaping. Through numerical simulations of the full circuit Hamiltonian, we demonstrate a bias-preserving CX gate achieving 99.69% fidelity in the absence of photon loss for a gate duration of 50 ns. Under a single-photon loss rate of 100 kHz, our protocol yields a noise bias of 9922, exceeding the noise bias of a naive non-bias-preserving CX implementation by approximately a factor of 570. These results support the ATS coupler as a valuable building block for concatenated cat-qubit architectures.

Kerem Yurtseven, Shantanu R. Jha, Apoorva Limaye, Risav Pokhrel, and Muhammad Waqar Amin

item.title: Engineering \(XY\) and \(ZZ\) interactions between two remote superconducting qubits via a multimode waveguide
item.author: Da-Wei Wang, and Yu-xi Liu
item.content:encoded:
Waveguides provide a flexible platform for long-range interactions between superconducting qubits. Here, we study how to engineer the effective (XY) and (ZZ) interactions betweentwo qubits via qubit frequency assignments and multimode interference determined by the mode configuration and standing-wave parities of a finite multimode waveguide. For a single-mode waveguide, we find that \(XY\) and \(ZZ\) interactions cannot be simultaneously suppressed to zero and the residual qubit-qubit coupling always exists. For example, the \(XY\) interaction may be suppressed to a negligible level when two qubits and the waveguide mode satisfy the two-photon resonant condition, but the \(ZZ\) interaction cannot be switched off. For multimode configurations within the central dispersive window, the engineered interaction types are very different for odd and even numbers of modes. Even-mode configurations can readily produce strong \(XY\) interactions, whereas odd-mode configurations can strongly suppress the \(XY\) interaction while retaining a finite \(ZZ\) interaction. Full-Hamiltonian simulations of minimal two- and three-mode configurations confirm \(XY\)-dominated SWAP dynamics and \(ZZ\)-dominated CZ-type dynamics, respectively. These results establish a frequency assignment criterion of qubits and waveguide modes for selectively engineering long-range qubit-qubit interaction types induced by the waveguide with finite multimode.

Da-Wei Wang, and Yu-xi Liu

item.title: Multimode Parametric Amplifier for K-Band Quantum Measurements
item.author: Chulwoo Ahn, and Vladimir Manucharyan
item.content:encoded:
We demonstrate K-band nondegenerate three-wave-mixing amplification in a multimode resonator comprising an array of 500 SNAILs. Pairing K-band signal modes with lower-frequency internalidler modes enables 20 dB of gain continuously from 19.6 to 25.6 GHz with pump frequencies below 32.2 GHz. At 20 dB gain, the 3-dB bandwidth ranges from 2.6 to 11.7 MHz, and the input-referred 1-dB compression power reaches -100.9 dBm. In the 20-22 GHz band, the average added noise is 0.73 quanta. A two-mode nondegenerate parametric amplification model describes the measured gain response and gain-bandwidth behavior, while a multimode Kerr model captures the overall compression scale. Our amplifier provides a practical solution for implementing a state-of-the-art readout of superconducting qubits in the K-band.

Chulwoo Ahn, and Vladimir Manucharyan

item.title: Controlled-Z Gates via Floquet Coupling to Two Auxiliary States in Transmon Circuits
item.author: Yutao Chen, Jia-Chi Zhang, Tian-Ming Li, Yu Liu, Kai Xu, and Heng Fan
item.content:encoded:
High-fidelity entangling gates are essential for quantum information processing. In transmon circuits, higher excited states provide additional pathways for engineering interactionswithin the computational subspace. Here we demonstrate controlled-Z (CZ) gates that exploit two noncomputational states, $\ket{02}$ and $\ket{20}$, through selective Floquet coupling. The nontrivial parametric modulation can activate both auxiliary transitions from $\ket{11}$ while suppressing the leading exchange between $\ket{01}$ and $\ket{10}$. Based on this approach, we develop two gate protocols: a nonadiabatic round trip through a bright auxiliary superposition and adiabatic evolution along a zero-energy dark state, both achieving average gate fidelities above 99.99% in numerical simulations. Control of the modulation phase further extends the bright-state protocol to conventional and unconventional geometric CZ gates. Effective-model simulations show that unconventional control improves tolerance to residual ZZ coupling and static qubit-frequency offsets relative to conventional control over the parameter ranges examined. Simulations including neighboring spectator qubits show that the original nonadiabatic bright-state and adiabatic dark-state CZ protocols retain high gate fidelities. This framework offers new routes toward the experimental realization of CZ gates and their geometric implementations.

Yutao Chen, Jia-Chi Zhang, Tian-Ming Li, Yu Liu, Kai Xu, and Heng Fan

item.title: Optimal Quantum-Circuit Synthesis and Implementation of General Unitaries with Parallelized Bitstring-Conditioned Rotations
item.author: Heikki Suominen, Suman Kundu, Heidi Kivijärvi, Sasu Tuohino, Mikko Tuokkola, Eemeli Forsbom, Madhavi Chand, Vasilii Vadimov, R. Vijay, and Mikko Möttönen
item.content:encoded:
We theoretically introduce a quantum-circuit synthesis protocol to realize any n-qubit transformation U∈U(2n), up to a diagonal. The resulting circuit is directly native to and optimalin gate count and depth for systems where bitstring-conditioned rotations with tunable angle and axis, C(n−1)R(θ,ϕ), form the set of native operations. Subsequently, we suggest how this protocol can be implemented in a few-mode superconducting circuit, and experimentally demonstrate the method for the smallest nontrivial case, i.e., for two qubits. We report an average gate fidelity of 97.6 % for Haar-random two-qubit unitaries up to phase shifts in the computational basis. Importantly, these results suggest that multimode devices, such as those in the multimon or multiunimon families may become competitive with qubit-array networks for general-unitary implementations for qubit counts as low as three.

Heikki Suominen, Suman Kundu, Heidi Kivijärvi, Sasu Tuohino, Mikko Tuokkola, Eemeli Forsbom, Madhavi Chand, Vasilii Vadimov, R. Vijay, and Mikko Möttönen

item.title: Sidewall Metrology Protocol for Superconducting Qubit Devices
item.author: Jørgen Garnæs, Henrik S. Guttesen, Astrid T. Rømer, Oscar Danielsson, Emily P. Duggan, Zhenhai Sun, Asen Lyubenov Georgiev, Li Wei Chang, Morten Kjaergaard, Mark Bieler, Lukas Grünhaupt, and Sabbir A. Khan
item.content:encoded:
Sidewall morphology is a potentially important factor influencing superconducting qubit performance, yet its quantitative characterization remains challenging due to the absence ofstandardized measurement protocols. In this work, we develop a scanning probe microscopy-based measurement framework for the quantitative characterization of superconducting qubit sidewalls. The framework introduces a refined root mean square lateral sidewall roughness descriptor and a new curvature-equivalent radius for quantifying vertical sidewall morphology. The descriptors and measurement procedures are applied to different components of qubit devices, forming the basis of a proposed sidewall characterization protocol. This provides a foundation for quantitative comparisons of fabrication processes across laboratories, enabling future investigations of correlations between sidewall geometry and qubit performance.

Jørgen Garnæs, Henrik S. Guttesen, Astrid T. Rømer, Oscar Danielsson, Emily P. Duggan, Zhenhai Sun, Asen Lyubenov Georgiev, Li Wei Chang, Morten Kjaergaard, Mark Bieler, Lukas Grünhaupt, and Sabbir A. Khan
